currentWork.title: Operational field use — FINAL.23 arbitrary task selection verified
currentWork.releaseStatus: FINAL.23 is merged and production verified. The fixed 'one vending machine' task mode from FINAL.22 was replaced by a true selection-type target: the operator can search and choose any number of individual vending machines, while the existing all/manufacturer-wide target mode remains available. Selected machines are shown as a removable list with a count before task creation. Prior single-machine/custom task targets migrate to selection-type semantics, and Task Detail add/remove keeps customized tasks as selection-type. Percentage auto-completion remains unchanged. PR #142 merged to main at 1243c091afba07ba7945f9fb7cf339cc515d0988. PR browser run 37321748627 and main run 37321896627 passed all five gates; GitHub Pages run 37321895075 and Vercel production status passed. Analytics engine/DB/schema remain AN14B3B5 / 4 / 4.
scope: Task target modes are manufacturer-based or selection-type; do not constrain selection-type to exactly one machine.
Selection-type task creation supports one or many arbitrary vending machines chosen via search.
Show selected machine count and allow removal before saving.
Keep existing all-manufacturer / one-manufacturer task targeting.
Migrate FINAL.22 single-machine/custom task target types to selection-type without losing targetMachineIds.
If Task Detail changes the target set, preserve the result as a selection-type task.
Keep the existing configurable 1–100% auto-completion threshold and exact ratio rule.
Keep task history, per-machine completion, visit task checks, order semantics, Analytics engine, DB and schema unchanged.
nextActions: Use selection-type task creation on the phone and confirm multiple arbitrary machines can be selected in one task.
Use manufacturer targeting when the entire manufacturer fleet is intended.
Reopen engineering only for new field friction or explicit product changes.

unresolved: Historical Analytics remains preserved and user-facing Analysis/OCR remains withdrawn; numeric learning promotion remains disabled.
